summary:
"Abandoned but Not Forgotten" is an interactive digital archive that explores the legacy of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through an engaging visual experience, the project allows users to discover historical space missions, explore abandoned spacecraft and scientific instruments, and understand the discoveries they made.
The platform combines interactive planetary exploration, a historical timeline, detailed artifact descriptions, and comparisons between lunar and Martian missions. It also categorizes equipment according to its current status, helping users understand which objects are still transmitting data, dormant, or have an unknown status.
The project addresses NASA's challenge by transforming space exploration history into an accessible and engaging learning experience, particularly for younger audiences. It highlights that even when a mission ends, its scientific contributions remain valuable. By preserving these stories, we can inspire curiosity about space, celebrate human ingenuity, and help future generations appreciate the legacy of space exploration.
details:
How it works

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive digital archive that allows users to explore human-made equipment left behind during space exploration. The website takes users on a journey across the Moon, Mars and deep space, where they can select glowing markers to discover individual spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments.

Each artifact has its own historical record, including its mission year, status, photographs and scientific significance. For example, users can explore NASA's Phoenix lander, which discovered water ice beneath the Martian surface in 2008. The platform also includes a mission log, an educational debrief with questions, source references and a child-friendly mode.

Benefits and intended impact

The project makes space exploration history more accessible, engaging and understandable. Instead of presenting abandoned equipment as forgotten objects, it highlights their scientific contributions and the knowledge they helped humanity gain. Its educational features aim to encourage curiosity, develop interest in science and engineering, and inspire younger generations to explore space-related careers.

Tools and technologies

The project was developed as a web-based interactive experience using Base44. It combines an interactive interface, visual planetary environments, historical information, photographs and educational elements. No additional physical hardware was required for development.

Creativity and originality

The creative idea behind the project is to turn abandoned space hardware into an explorable archive rather than a traditional historical list or article. The planetary interface allows users to discover objects geographically and interact with their stories. The combination of atmospheric space visuals, interactive markers, historical records and educational activities creates an experience that connects exploration, technology and storytelling.

Factors considered during development

Several factors guided the project:

  • Accessibility: Information should be understandable to people with different levels of scientific knowledge.
  • Education: Historical facts should be presented in an engaging way that encourages further learning.
  • Scientific relevance: The archive should highlight the actual missions, equipment and discoveries.
  • Visual experience: The interface should make exploring the Moon and Mars intuitive and interesting.
  • Preservation: The project should communicate why equipment left behind in space remains important to scientific history.

Ultimately, Abandoned but Not Forgotten aims to remind people that a space mission does not lose its importance when communication ends or equipment stops functioning. Its discoveries and contributions remain part of humanity's exploration story.
